title: International Economic Institutions: The Bretton Woods System and Beyond

questions.question: The Bretton Woods conference of 1944 gave birth to:
options: The IMF and the World Bank
questions.rationale: The 1944 conference (44 nations, Keynes and White as architects) created the IMF for monetary cooperation and the IBRD/World Bank for reconstruction. GATT arrived in 1947 and the WTO only in 1995.

questions.question: Which institution lends to countries facing balance-of-payments crises?
questions.rationale: The IMF is the short-run firefighter: standby arrangements and extended facilities provide foreign exchange in BoP distress, typically with policy conditionality. The World Bank funds long-run development; the WTO makes trade rules and does not lend.

questions.question: Voting power in the IMF is determined by:
questions.rationale: A member's quota - its subscription - sets its vote, borrowing access and SDR allocation, concentrating influence in large economies. The WTO by contrast operates on consensus with formal one-member-one-vote equality.

questions.question: The Special Drawing Right (SDR) is:
options: The IMF's reserve asset based on a basket of major currencies
The World Bank's unit of account
questions.rationale: The SDR is a basket of five currencies (USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, GBP) allocated to IMF members to supplement reserves - expanded by $650 billion in 2021 during the pandemic.

questions.question: Which arm of the World Bank Group provides interest-free credits to the poorest countries?
questions.rationale: The International Development Association (1960) extends concessional, essentially interest-free finance to low-income countries. IBRD lends to middle-income governments, IFC to private firms, MIGA guarantees against political risk, ICSID arbitrates disputes.

questions.question: The WTO was established in:
questions.rationale: The Uruguay Round's final act created the WTO on 1 January 1995, upgrading the 1947 GATT into a full institution with services (GATS), IP (TRIPS) and binding dispute settlement.

questions.question: The most-favoured-nation (MFN) principle requires that:
options: Any trade concession to one member be extended to all members
Imports be taxed more than domestic goods
questions.rationale: MFN is non-discrimination: favour one, favour all. National treatment - the companion rule - then forbids taxing imports worse than domestic goods once they have entered.

questions.question: The WTO's Appellate Body, the crown of its dispute settlement system, has been paralysed since 2019 because:
options: The US has blocked appointments to it
The Doha Round merged it with the IMF
questions.rationale: Blocking new appointments leaves the seven-member body without a quorum, so appeals lapse into the void. Members responded with the interim multi-party appeal arrangement and, increasingly, unilateral retaliation.

questions.question: The IMF's conditionality refers to:
options: Policy adjustments attached to loans above the basic tranche
questions.rationale: Access to larger IMF programs requires agreed policy measures - fiscal tightening, exchange-rate reform, structural changes - intended to restore external viability. Critics blame these austerity conditions for deepening crises such as the 1997-98 Asian turmoil.

questions.question: Which pairing of flagship publication and institution is correct?
questions.rationale: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook (and Fiscal Monitor); the World Bank publishes the World Development Report (and published Doing Business until 2021). The WTO's signature output is its agreements and the World Trade Report.
